thread:
elaine: Heads up — Vector Systems (HW SI) wants a Datadog + OpenTelemetry integration as part of their on‑prem appliance marketplace listing. Need a short ops checklist and owners. Target: next Friday for joint demo.

samir: Ok — do we want OTLP gRPC to collector on the appliance, or push from our side?

maria: Prefer appliance -> OTLP collector (local) so customers can keep traces inside their network. We'll need an example collector config & dashboard bundle.

paul: Sales needs two slides for the deck: what metrics/traces look like, and what support level is included. Can eng produce a minimal example app trace?

elaine: @samir can you own the example trace and a small instrumented app? @maria takes dashboard + datadog agent config. @jen to own marketplace asset packaging and announcement coord.

samir: I can build a tiny inference shim that emits spans: key attrs = model_id, request_id, batch_size, seq_len, kv_cache_hits. Also emit per-token latency and end_to_end_latency. Planning to instrument using OpenTelemetry Python.

samir: snippet for OTLP env we plan to include in shipper docs:
```bash
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4317
export OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.name=vector-infer,deployment.environment=onprem
```

maria: For Datadog agent on appliance we should recommend the agent + otlp receiver forwarding to DD: config example:
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
exporters:
  datadog:
    apikey: <REDACTED_FROM_TEMPLATE>
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [datadog]
```

jenn: small note — we cannot include real API keys in marketplace assets. Use template placeholders and a snippet referencing our docs page.

maria: Dashboard checklist:
- GPU metrics: gpu.util, gpu.mem.used, gpu.temperature
- Inference metrics: request.count, request.latency.p50/p95, tokens.generated.count
- Traces: span breakdown, e2e latency, kernel queue time (if available)
- Alert templates: high tail latency, GPU OOM, trace error rate

paul: Do we have an owner for canary testing during the demo? Need to verify OTLP traces actually make it into Datadog and dashboards show model_id tag.

samir: I'll run the canary on our staging on Thursday. Will post logs.

deploy-bot: deploy: instrumentation-demo v0.1 deployed to staging (tag: vector-demo-2026-03-20) :rocket:

maria: For the marketplace tile we should include a 1‑minute GIF of the dashboard updating + a short troubleshooting section (collector diagnostics, agent status commands). I'll draft the README.

elaine: Timelines:
- Samir: instrumented app + sample traces by Wed EOD
- Maria: dashboard JSON + agent/collector snippets by Thu noon
- Jen: marketplace assets draft and PR by Thu EOD
- Paul: deck slides once we have assets, Fri morning runway for demo

paul: 👍 added to calendar invite. Who's presenting infra in the demo? @elaine?

elaine: I'll do infra + fallback policy. Samir will demo trace-driven debugging. Maria you show dashboards. Jen will cover packaging/announcement.

samir: One more ask — can we surface model version in the trace/span and as a tag in Datadog APM? That will be critical for rollback analysis.

maria: yes — we will map span attribute `model.version` -> Datadog tag `model_version` in the collector rewrite rule example.

jen: I'll coordinate PR reviews with legal for the announcement language (no partner logos until approvals). Also confirm Vector Systems' marketing lead tomorrow.

elaine: Great. I'll follow up with a short RFC PR that ties these pieces together. Thanks team :thumbsup:

samir: I'll drop the repo link when the demo app is up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/vector-observability-demo

maria: Draft dashboard JSON will be posted to the PR. After review, we can export the Datadog dashboard template for the marketplace bundle.

paul: Anything else?

jen: One small ops note — remind Vector to open port 4317 on the appliance control plane to allow local OTLP gRPC. We'll add that to the preflight checklist.

elaine: Noted. Closing actions in the RFC. Thanks everyone! :white_check_mark:
